requirements.requirement: Configure node1, node2, node3 as a three-member Galera cluster where writes on any member are visible from the others
requirements.summary: Node1 was bootstrapped with --wsrep-new-cluster, node2 and node3 joined via rsync SST, and wsrep_cluster_size reached 3 with wsrep_local_state_comment=Synced on all nodes (cmd-113019f72eb54549). Distinct rows inserted from node1, node2, and node3 into galeratest.t were each confirmed visible on the other nodes, culminating in all three rows visible on node1 (cmd-592954938eb34643, cmd-2476a0ed920b4641, cmd-18e60fc5de644e61, cmd-657c3859fc1f4dcf), directly demonstrating multi-master replication across all three members.

requirements.requirement: Database remains available (accepts writes) when one member is unavailable
requirements.summary: node2 was stopped via rc-service (cmd-6e6edee7dfb2426d). While it was down, node1 showed wsrep_cluster_size=2/status=Primary and successfully inserted a row (cmd-e1a2839e49f34f23), and node3 also inserted a row and read consistent data including node1's write (cmd-ebdd91dc269d4b6c). This directly demonstrates continued write availability under a bounded 2/3-quorum disruption.

node2 was restarted via plain rc-service start with no manual SST/state intervention (cmd-be61685380a34a70). It immediately reported wsrep_local_state_comment=Synced, cluster_size=3, and returned all 5 rows including the two written while it was offline, directly showing automatic resynchronization.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on every managed node (independent of the public task contract)
requirements.summary: For all three nodes, a pre-restart baseline (boot_id, Synced/Primary/size-3, row count) was captured, a native 'reboot' was issued, the node became unreachable and then responsive again with a different boot_id and uptime reset to 0, and post-reboot queries showed Synced/Primary/size-3 with full data recovery including rows written while each node was offline (node1: cmd-fec4e2f1b2ed4ec2/cmd-a28512fe864d476b/cmd-4a6e343914104139/cmd-96f79de095174612/cmd-ffcf3d5054504b16; node2: cmd-50187bc14fe24d01/cmd-22230beab2254dab/cmd-9ce1c4dfa26f479c/cmd-df3b73b7f8544147/cmd-d26e8cef68de4696; node3: cmd-a6fe2765ede14727/cmd-bf6dfd24963e40b3/cmd-d4cc8f273a6f4ac6/cmd-bb8e090f5ee244c0). A final cross-node consistency check confirmed cluster_size=3, Primary, Synced, and identical row count (7) everywhere (cmd-b9054bce6cd74de6, cmd-8a732c8906dc4ed7, cmd-08945559af724288). The fixed after-prepare and after-executor boot-identity snapshots independently corroborate the pre/post boot_id values reported in the command timeline for all three nodes.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the public task contract are satisfied with direct, observed evidence: a working 3-node Galera cluster with confirmed multi-master write visibility, demonstrated write availability during a bounded single-node outage, and demonstrated automatic resynchronization on rejoin. The independent provider-wide restart protocol was also executed and evidenced completely and coherently for all three nodes, cross-checked against the fixed boot-identity snapshots. The path to this end state involved substantial troubleshooting flailing (Alpine-specific SST tooling issues) including one notably risky self-inflicted disconnect/rebuild of node1 and some unremoved temporary artifacts, which are reflected in a moderate operational hygiene score, but none of this undermines the final functional outcome.
limitations: The command timeline shows many failed/aborted intermediate attempts (SST failures, crashed mariadb states, non-Primary views) before the cluster stabilized; while none of these misrepresent the final state, they indicate the deployment process was not clean or idempotent.

The root password is stored in plaintext files (/root/.mariadb_root_pw) on all three nodes; this is outside the stated task requirements so it does not affect functional scoring but is a minor operational note.

No evidence was captured of behavior under two simultaneous node failures or of behavior if the SST/network is partitioned asymmetrically; only single-node disruption and sequential single-node reboots were tested, consistent with the task's stated requirement of tolerating one unavailable member.

operational_hygiene.summary: Extensive troubleshooting was required to get rsync SST working on Alpine (busybox lsof/ps limitations), which is legitimate diagnostic work, but several state-changing actions along the way exceeded bounded troubleshooting and left residue or caused unnecessary disruption. Most notably, on node1 the executor ran 'SET GLOBAL wsrep_provider_options=...' (failed, read-only) followed by 'SET GLOBAL wsrep_cluster_address="gcomm://"' (cmd-0d13e6b8b6c94519), which deliberately disconnected the sole functioning cluster node from replication (cluster_size dropped to 0), forcing a full shutdown, datadir wipe, and from-scratch cluster rebuild (cmd-b5f981429e014131, cmd-93a4f46bb5e84253, cmd-395844e02a424c0f) — a broad, self-inflicted mutation with no clear necessity, though it was fully recovered from and did not persist. Ad-hoc rsync daemon test/kill cycles on node2 (cmd-b47d6c0ce1ff4930, cmd-8cebbb09eeea4c0c, cmd-1fb8b1e29ae24f45) were bounded, low-risk, and reverted via pkill. Minor residue was left in the final state: temporary log files (/tmp/mysqld_boot.log, /tmp/reboot.log, /tmp/rsynctest.log) visible in the after-executor snapshot, and the ad-hoc 'galeratest' test database/table were not cleaned up. No failed services, broken package state, or weakened security controls beyond the SST design choice of an empty wsrep_sst_auth (inherent to the rsync SST method) were observed.
